avoid_hardcode.policy: Domain rules, thresholds, source authority, feature weights, phase policies, chip rules, finance rules, scoring constants, scheduler cadence, service boundaries, wire profiles, payload projection contracts, materialization policy and performance budgets must be config/registry driven unless a literal is structurally intrinsic to the implementation.
avoid_hardcode.exceptions: Any unavoidable hardcoded value must be documented with rationale, owner, and test coverage.

modular_authority.policy: If a domain can reasonably be separated into a dedicated module or registry, V5 does so by default whenever separation improves identification, adjustment, authority clarity, provenance, testing, maintenance, or reuse. Consumers depend on the shared authority instead of duplicating logic.
modular_authority.performance_guard: Do not create runtime fragmentation that causes material latency regression. Prefer cached registries and stable module boundaries over repeated file reads, duplicated transforms, or excessive indirection.
modular_authority.discoverability: Every separated domain is registered in config/v5_module_registry.json with its plane, entrypoint, controlling config, status, and adjustment surface.

microservices.policy: V5 production runtime must execute as independently runnable bounded-context services. A monorepo and shared immutable image are allowed, but business domains must not collapse back into one process or duplicate authority across services.
requirements: unique service ownership of business modules
connection reuse for internal HTTP transport
runtime materialization must preserve durable persistence authority
non-idempotent persistence operations are never automatically retried
parallel fan-out for independent service calls
microservices.performance_guard: Use bounded contexts rather than per-function services. Avoid chatty service graphs, batch large reads, parallelize independent intelligence services, cache immutable registry data, reuse internal HTTP connections, use compact registry-selected wire codecs and payload projections for large internal payloads, materialize same-run artifacts without bypassing durable writes, and measure cross-service latency including retry overhead.

performance_first.policy: Every material V5 change must be evaluated for correctness and processing speed. Prefer single-pass transforms, bounded candidate universes, cached immutable lookups, batched/parallel operations where useful, compact versioned transport contracts, and avoid repeated network or file reads.
performance_first.acceptance: Performance regression beyond configured budgets blocks promotion unless explicitly reviewed.
